note: Attacker-controlled raw JPEG bytes are read from the environment variable and passed to the fuzzer entry point.
A buffer is allocated to hold the input JPEG data for the transform operations.
The raw attacker-controlled JPEG bytes are copied into srcBuf, which is then passed to tjTransform().

First tjTransform() call with TJXOP_NONE, TJXOPT_PROGRESSIVE|TJXOPT_COPYNONE, and TJFLAG_LIMITSCANS|TJFLAG_NOREALLOC. This reads coefficients from the input JPEG and writes them to a progressive JPEG output.
The JPEG header is parsed. If the input is truncated or malformed, the decompressor may not fully initialize all coefficient blocks.

Coefficient arrays are read from the source JPEG. For truncated or incomplete scan data, some coefficient blocks may remain at their initial (zeroed) state, but the transform workspace arrays are not pre-zeroed.
Workspace coefficient arrays are allocated with pre_zero=FALSE in transupp.c, meaning they are not initialized to zero before the transform routine writes to them.

The workspace virtual barray is requested with pre_zero=FALSE. If the transform routine does not write every block (e.g., due to incomplete source data or edge cases), uninitialized memory remains in the destination coefficient array.
The transform is executed. For JXFORM_NONE with no crop, no workspace is needed and the source coefficient arrays are used directly as the destination.

The destination coefficient arrays are passed to the compressor. If any coefficient block contains uninitialized values (because the source JPEG had incomplete scan data and the workspace was not pre-zeroed), the encoder will read from uninitialized memory.
compress_output reads coefficient blocks from the virtual barray and passes them to the entropy encoder. Blocks that were never written by the transform contain uninitialized values.
The sequential Huffman encoder processes each coefficient block. The block contains uninitialized coefficient values from the incomplete source data.

encode_one_block reads the DC coefficient from the block. If the block was never initialized (due to incomplete scan data and non-pre-zeroed workspace), this reads uninitialized memory, triggering the Use-of-uninitialized-value sanitizer report.
